systemic_drivers.name: Infrastructure and power instability
systemic_drivers.description: Unreliable power supply, load shedding, and lack of backup generation in rural health facilities directly interrupt diagnostic services and cold-chain integrity.

examples: laboratory centrifuge / automated analyzer power loss
temperature-controlled reagent or vaccine storage failure

sources.source_name: Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) Guidelines - MoHFW

potential_consequences: Inability to perform confirmatory diagnostic tests on-site
Compromised reagent quality due to cold-chain disruption
referral_implications: Patients with suspected severe illness may require referral to facilities with functional emergency backup power.

source_refs.source_name: IPHS Guidelines for Primary & Community Health Centres - MoHFW

systemic_drivers.name: Symptom-centric care under limited diagnostic access
systemic_drivers.description: When point-of-care diagnostic testing or laboratory workups are unavailable or delayed, clinicians may rely on empirical symptomatic management. Limited diagnostic information increases clinical uncertainty in undifferentiated presentations.

examples: Empirical antipyretic or antibiotic administration for undifferentiated acute febrile illness
Analgesic management for persistent abdominal pain without ultrasound/lab confirmation

sources.source_name: ICMR Guidelines for Antimicrobial Stewardship in Primary Care

potential_consequences: Masking of progressive symptoms during empirical supportive care
Delay in establishing definitive diagnosis for conditions mimicking common acute syndromes
referral_implications: Persistent or non-responsive symptoms despite supportive care warrant escalation for diagnostic evaluation.

source_refs.source_name: ICMR Guidelines for Antimicrobial Stewardship in Primary Care

systemic_drivers.name: Limited specialist referral pathways and tertiary access
systemic_drivers.description: Geographic distance, transport limitations, and scarcity of resident specialists (neurology, orthopaedics, general/trauma surgery) at primary/secondary levels create delays in definitive higher-level evaluation.

examples: Delayed surgical evaluation for acute abdomen or complicated trauma
Delayed neurological imaging and evaluation for head injury or stroke

sources.source_name: NITI Aayog - Primary Health Care Insights

potential_consequences: Prolonged transit or waiting times for tertiary evaluation
Need for early risk stratification and pre-transfer stabilization at local facilities
referral_implications: Time-sensitive conditions require early identification and emergency transport mobilization rather than local observation.

source_refs.source_name: NITI Aayog - Primary Health Care Insights

conditions.description: Tuberculous spondylitis affecting the vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs. Characterized by insidious onset back pain, systemic symptoms, and potential neurological compression.
diagnosis: spine X-ray (narrowed disc space, vertebral destruction)
treatment: Surgical decompression when severe neurological deficit is present
conditions.referral_relevance: Requires radiological imaging and specialist orthopedic/neurosurgical evaluation. Neurological deficits demand urgent higher-level referral.

diagnostic_risks: Early subtle vertebral changes may not be apparent on basic radiography
Insidious onset back pain may be managed empirically without imaging workup
systemic_constraints: MRI and specialized spine CT are unavailable at primary facility level
Long duration of ATT requires treatment adherence support

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Both present with lower back pain. Early spinal TB lacks overt neurological signs and may mimic mechanical or muscular strain.
distinguishing_information: Chronicity (>3-4 weeks)
Nocturnal pain / pain unrelieved by rest
Constitutional features (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Localized spinal bony tenderness

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Nerve root compression from tuberculous abscess or collapse mimics lumbar disc prolapse.
distinguishing_information: Systemic constitutional symptoms
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR)
Vertebral destruction on imaging

sources.source_name: National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) Technical Guidelines - MoHFW

conditions.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection primarily involving the lungs. Characterized by persistent cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.
treatment: Standard anti-tubercular therapy regimens under NTEP
conditions.referral_relevance: Requires diagnostic confirmation via Truenat/CBNAAT or sputum microscopy and chest X-ray.

diagnostic_risks: Persistent cough may initially be treated empirically with antibiotics or cough suppressants
systemic_constraints: Truenat / CBNAAT testing may require sample transport to block/district facility

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Both present with persistent respiratory symptoms and cough.
distinguishing_information: Episodic wheezing and reversibility in asthma vs progressive constitutional decline in TB
Fever, night sweats, and weight loss characteristic of TB
Sputum microbiological positivity in TB

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Chronic cough in smokers or biomass-fuel exposed individuals can mask active pulmonary TB.
distinguishing_information: Recent change in cough character or onset of evening fever
Microbiological sputum testing (CBNAAT/smear)

sources.source_name: National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) Guidelines - MoHFW

conditions.description: Persistently elevated systemic arterial blood pressure (systolic >= 140 or diastolic >= 90 mmHg).
diagnosis: basic lab screening for organ involvement
conditions.referral_relevance: Hypertensive crisis or organ dysfunction requires urgent higher-level evaluation.

diagnostic_risks: Nonspecific symptoms like fatigue or mild headache may be attributed to general strain rather than checked for elevated BP
systemic_constraints: Opportunistic BP screening at primary encounters is essential to detect asymptomatic cases

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Nonspecific fatigue or weakness is a common chief complaint that overlaps with many conditions; without BP measurement, hypertension may remain undetected.
distinguishing_information: Objective blood pressure measurement confirms or excludes elevated BP

source_refs.source_name: NPCDCS Guidelines for NCD Screening - MoHFW

sources.source_name: National Programme for Prevention & Control of Cancer, Diabetes, CVD & Stroke (NPCDCS) - MoHFW

conditions.description: Metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia resulting from insulin resistance and progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction.
diagnosis: Random plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL with symptoms
conditions.referral_relevance: Diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar state, or severe foot infection requires urgent referral.

diagnostic_risks: Nonspecific fatigue or recurrent skin infections may be treated symptomatically without checking blood glucose
systemic_constraints: Glucometer strip supply and HbA1c testing availability varies at sub-centre level

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Thirst, polyuria, and lethargy during hot weather may be assumed to be simple heat strain or dehydration.
distinguishing_information: Blood glucose testing (fasting or random) provides objective confirmation

conditions.description: Peripheral vestibular disorder caused by canalithiasis in the semicircular canals, causing brief, intense vertigo triggered by head position changes.
symptoms: vertigo triggered by rolling in bed or tilting head back
conditions.referral_relevance: Persistent positional vertigo or presence of red-flag neurological signs requires specialist evaluation.

diagnostic_risks: Episodic vertigo may be empirically attributed to cervical spondylosis or generalized weakness without positional testing
systemic_constraints: Dix-Hallpike positional examination is a bedside clinical maneuver that requires no equipment

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Dizziness or lightheadedness on neck movement is often attributed to cervical spondylosis, though BPPV is triggered specifically by head orientation relative to gravity.
distinguishing_information: Dix-Hallpike maneuver eliciting transient rotatory nystagmus
Brief duration (<60 seconds) per attack in BPPV
Absence of persistent neck stiffness as primary driver of vertigo

source_refs.source_name: DGHS Clinical Practice Guidelines for Primary Care

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Postural dizziness or lightheadedness in anemic patients can overlap with complaint of vertigo.
distinguishing_information: True spinning sensation (rotatory vertigo) in BPPV vs postural faintness in severe anemia
Hemoglobin estimation for anemia confirmation

sources.source_name: Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) Guidelines - MoHFW

conditions.description: Common mental health conditions characterized by persistent low mood, loss of interest, excessive worry, or physical somatic manifestations.
symptoms: loss of interest in daily activities
diagnosis: Clinical psychiatric evaluation / PHQ-9 / GAD-7 screening
Exclusion of organic systemic causes (thyroid, anemia, chronic infection)
conditions.referral_relevance: Severe depression with suicidal ideation or psychosis requires urgent psychiatric referral.

diagnostic_risks: Mental health distress frequently presents with somatic complaints (e.g. fatigue, headache, weakness) which may undergo repeated physical workups
systemic_constraints: Mental health specialist availability (District Mental Health Programme / Tele-MANAS) varies at primary level

somatic_phrases: taaqat ki kami (weakness / lack of physical energy)
cultural_context.notes: Culturally expressed somatic phrases are common ways individuals describe emotional distress. Note: Supernatural beliefs (e.g. evil eye) may influence community help-seeking but are not medical causes.

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Depressive distress often presents as physical exhaustion or generalized pain ('taaqat ki kami').
distinguishing_information: Structured mood and anxiety inquiry (PHQ-2 / PHQ-9 screening)
Absence of localized organic lesion after basic screening

source_refs.source_name: District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) Guidelines - MoHFW

sources.source_name: District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) / Tele-MANAS Framework - MoHFW

conditions.description: Protozoan infection transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. Causes acute febrile illness with potential for severe complication (severe anemia, cerebral malaria, organ failure).
symptoms: acute fever with chills and rigors
conditions.referral_relevance: Severe malaria (cerebral signs, jaundice, acute kidney injury, severe anemia) requires immediate emergency referral.

diagnostic_risks: Acute febrile illness in endemic areas requires rapid testing to distinguish malaria from dengue, typhoid, or scrub typhus
systemic_constraints: RDT kit supply and trained microscopy personnel at sub-centre / PHC level

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Both present as acute febrile illness with severe body ache, headache, and fatigue.
distinguishing_information: RDT / blood smear for Plasmodium antigen / parasite vs Dengue NS1 / IgM serology
Thrombocytopenia and hemoconcentration prominent in Dengue
Periodic fever spikes with rigors typical of Malaria

source_refs.source_name: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) Guidelines

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Both present as high fever with systemic toxicity in endemic areas.
distinguishing_information: Step-ladder fever pattern, abdominal discomfort, bradycardia in Typhoid
Malaria RDT / smear confirmation

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Acute febrile illness with headache and myalgia following vegetation exposure.
distinguishing_information: Presence of an eschar (punched-out ulcer with black crust) in Scrub Typhus
Scrub typhus IgM ELISA / RDT vs Malaria RDT

source_refs.source_name: NCDC Guidelines on Diagnosis & Management of Scrub Typhus

sources.source_name: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) - MoHFW

conditions.description: Inflammation of the vermiform appendix. May present as classical acute RLQ pain or sub-acute atypical abdominal discomfort.
symptoms: periumbilical pain migrating to Right Lower Quadrant (RLQ)
conditions.referral_relevance: Requires urgent surgical evaluation and ultrasound imaging; risk of perforation and peritonitis.

diagnostic_risks: Early or atypical sub-acute presentations may be managed empirically as gastritis or indigestion
systemic_constraints: Ultrasound imaging and emergency surgical capability are available at CHC / District Hospital level

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: Early appendicitis pain originates in the epigastrium or periumbilical area, mimicking dyspepsia or gastritis.
distinguishing_information: Migration of pain to the Right Lower Quadrant over 6-24 hours
Localized RLQ tenderness on palpation (McBurney's sign)
Fever and leukocytosis on CBC

source_refs.source_name: DGHS Manual of Emergency Surgical Procedures

diagnostic_confusion.why_confusion_can_occur: In females of childbearing age, lower abdominal pain and fever overlap between PID and appendicitis.
distinguishing_information: Bilateral vs localized RLQ tenderness
Vaginal discharge / cervical motion tenderness in PID
Pelvic ultrasound evaluation

sources.source_name: DGHS Clinical Guidelines for Surgical Emergencies - MoHFW

injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: Without gross deformity or cortical displacement, undisplaced fractures present with localized pain and swelling that closely resembles a severe sprain. Scaphoid fractures in particular may not show cortical disruption on initial plain radiography.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: Plain X-ray imaging (including scaphoid view) is essential; repeat radiography in 10-14 days or immobilization if clinical anatomical snuffbox tenderness persists.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Persistent anatomical tenderness or inability to bear weight despite 1-2 weeks of conservative sprain management warrants repeat radiograph or orthopedic referral.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Non-urgent orthopedic referral for persistent focal bony tenderness; immobilization recommended at primary level.

source_refs.source_name: National Trauma Care Management Guidelines - MoHFW

injury_diagnostic_risks.canonical_name: Blunt Abdominal Trauma & Internal Organ Injury
injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: External abdominal appearance may show minimal bruising even in the presence of significant solid organ laceration (spleen/liver) or retroperitoneal bleeding. Compensation in young individuals can conceal early intra-abdominal hemorrhage.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: FAST ultrasound scan (Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma) and serial hemoglobin/vitals monitoring are critical.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Development of abdominal distension, tachycardia, hypotension, or shoulder tip pain (Kehr's sign) indicates ongoing internal bleeding.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Level 4 Emergency Referral required when mechanism of injury is high-energy or signs of internal hemorrhage / FAST positivity appear.

injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: Elevated intra-compartmental pressure compromises tissue perfusion. Early signs (severe pain out of proportion to injury, pain on passive stretch) may be mistaken for expected post-fracture swelling.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: Clinical diagnosis based on the 6 Ps: Pain out of proportion, Passive stretch pain, Paresthesia, Pallor, Paralysis, Pulselessness (late). Measurement of compartment pressure if available.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Time-sensitive surgical emergency — irreversible nerve and muscle necrosis occurs within 6 hours.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Immediate Level 4 emergency referral to a facility with surgical/orthopedic capability for urgent fasciotomy.

injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: Acute joint effusion and pain mask ligament laxity during initial physical exam. Achilles tendon rupture can be missed if plantarflexion by deep flexors is mistaken for intact tendon.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: Thompson squeeze test for Achilles tendon; stress testing and MRI for knee ligaments. Plain X-ray rules out avulsion fractures.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Persistent joint instability ('giving way') or inability to raise on toes after acute trauma.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Elective to urgent orthopedic evaluation depending on acute functional deficit.

injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: Initial mild presentation after head trauma (brief loss of consciousness or transient confusion) may be dismissed, while expanding intracranial hematoma develops over subsequent hours.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: Non-contrast CT scan of the brain is the definitive diagnostic modality for acute intracranial bleeding.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Warning signs (vomiting, worsening headache, unequal pupils, drowsiness, focal deficit, seizure) indicate expanding mass lesion.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Level 4 Emergency Referral required when head trauma is accompanied by LOC, vomiting, or neurological signs.

injury_diagnostic_risks.why_difficult_clinically: Fang marks may be faint or hidden. Early neurotoxic signs (bilateral ptosis, diplopia) or early hemotoxic signs (local swelling, bleeding from puncture site) may be subtle.
injury_diagnostic_risks.imaging_or_diagnostic_relevance: 20-Minute Whole Blood Clotting Test (20WBCT) at bedside for hemotoxicity. Clinical monitoring for cranial nerve palsies.
injury_diagnostic_risks.persistence_or_worsening_warning: Rapid progression of neuroparalysis or systemic bleeding. Requires immediate ASV administration.
injury_diagnostic_risks.referral_urgency_relevance: Level 4 Emergency Referral to an ASV-capable facility with emergency airway / ventilator support.
